abandon: m08 needs the RL delta to add a roughly fixed amount to the per-token log-odds of closing, whatever the host. Under its own exponential-hazard reading (P(cap) = exp(-h * 16,384), so ln h moves by the same amount in every host for the same dose), the board already says no. (1) The same full delta at a = 1 moves the two hosts very differently. Base -> RL: result-82b4dc 'base+cue 164/328 (50.0 %, 77 cap hits), RL 206/328 (62.8 %, 20 cap hits)'; RL is base + 1.0(RL - base), so ln h rises by ln(ln(328/20)/ln(328/77)) = 0.66. Think-SFT -> Think-SFT + 1.0(RL - base): result-3387ce 'cap hits 94.5, 75, 54, 44, 33 for a = 0..4', so ln h rises by ln(ln(328/75)/ln(328/94.5)) = 0.17. That is about 4 times less, not a fixed amount. (2) The two curves bend in opposite directions. Think-SFT's ln h rises 0.17, 0.20, 0.11, 0.13 per unit of a, which slows down. The base's finish dial (result-6f1bb7 '-1 118/96; base 164/77; 0.5 170/50; 1 192/46; 1.5 203/25', then '2 190/5') rises 0.30, 0.54, 0.97 per unit of a over 0->1, 1->1.5, 1.5->2, which speeds up. A fixed shift per unit of dose would make both straight lines, and the first_test's own R^2 >= 0.9 linearity is already in doubt. (3) The hosts' own hazards are too close to need double the dose. At a = 0, cap hits are 77 of 328 (base, cue) against 94.5 of 328 (Think-SFT); over 4 samples, result-fc7efc gives 'Cap hits: RL 114, base 286, Think-SFT 378'. With a fixed shift, Think-SFT needs only ln(1.449/1.244) = 0.15 more in ln h to reach any cap level the base reaches. That is about a quarter of the base's shift per unit dose, nowhere near twice the dose. (4) The ratio being explained compares two different vectors and an unresolved peak. The base peak is for the top-8 directions, not the full delta that Think-SFT got. result-6f1bb7 says itself that '1.5 was one of seven sizes tried' and '203 at size 1.5 against 192 at size 1 is +3.4 pts [-0.9, 7.6]', so 'peaks near 1.5' is not established. On the Think-SFT side, the a = 2 optimum was chosen on the 328 itself (result-3387ce: 'The coefficient was chosen on the 328 itself'). A theory built on transferring a fixed log-odds dose between hosts would spend tests on a premise the stored cap-hit counts already refute: the same delta buys the base about 4 times more ending hazard than it buys Think-SFT. Caveat: the RL reference in (1) is RL plain (206/20); RL cue scores 205 and its cap-hit count is not on the board.
